subject: crow
title: Crows Make Decisions Twice as Fast as Humans, in 235 Milliseconds

scenes.text: A crow has no layered cortex. It still decides faster than you.
In Germany, carrion crows watched dots moving across a touchscreen.
They had to peck left or right, depending on where most of the dots were heading.
Average answer: 235 milliseconds. Humans and monkeys take about twice as long on similar tasks.
Their neurons had picked a direction just 70 milliseconds after the dots appeared.
Scientists think flying and grabbing food with a beak demanded a brain this fast.

description:
Crows make visual decisions about twice as fast as humans and monkeys.
In a University of Tübingen study published in Science, carrion crows judged the direction of moving dots in 235 milliseconds on average, with brain signals showing the choice about 70 milliseconds in.
Do you think you could beat a crow?
thumbnail_text: 235 MS. TWICE AS FAST AS YOU
first_comment: When the motion was clear, the crows were close to 100 percent accurate. What's the smartest thing you've ever seen a crow do?
